title: Trading Policy

tiers.name: Employees
tiers.description: All Directors of the Company, Group employees and contractors engaged by the Group. Bound by the general restrictions in section 4: no dealing with inside information, the Front Page Test, hedging ban (pre-vesting/holding lock), no dealing in other companies' securities with inside information, absolute margin lending ban, and no short-term/speculative dealing.

tiers.name: Restricted Persons
tiers.description: Directors of the Company, other key management personnel including the CEO & Managing Director and CEO direct reports (Senior Executives), and other persons who regularly possess inside information and have been advised by the General Counsel & Joint Company Secretary that they are subject to special restrictions (Nominated Employees). Also subject to blackout periods, the section 5.3 preclearance requirement for all other dealing, and obligations regarding their Connected Persons.

tiers.name: CEO or Chairman of the Board
tiers.description: The CEO & Managing Director or the Chairman of the Board; distinguished only for clearance purposes, approved by the Board.

tiers.name: Other Directors
tiers.description: Directors other than the CEO or Chairman; distinguished only for clearance purposes, approved by the Chairman and one other independent director.

tiers.name: Sales Team
tiers.description: Members of the Sales Team who are Restricted Persons; distinguished only for clearance purposes, approved by the Chief Commercial Officer.

tiers.name: Chief Commercial Officer
tiers.description: The Chief Commercial Officer; distinguished only for clearance purposes, approved by the CEO.

tiers.name: Other Restricted Persons
tiers.description: Any Restricted Person not falling into the other approval categories; distinguished only for clearance purposes, approved by the General Counsel & Joint Company Secretary.

tiers.name: Connected Persons
tiers.description: A family member who may be expected to influence, or be influenced by, the Restricted Person (spouse, partner, children, partner's children, or dependants), or a company or other entity the Restricted Person can control. Restricted Persons must ensure Connected Persons only deal in circumstances in which the Restricted Person would themselves be permitted to deal.

definitions.hedging_definition: entering into any arrangements that operate to limit the economic risk associated with holding the Company's securities

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Board may specify any other blackout period from time to time (5.1). No confidentiality requirement is stated for a Board-imposed additional blackout period itself, but if a dealing request is refused or an approval revoked, that fact must be kept confidential (5.4(c)).

rules.detail: Flat ban on speculative dealing including short-selling for all Employees; no vesting distinction and no clearance route.
rules.evidence: All Employees must not deal in the Company's securities on a speculative basis, including short-selling. Short selling involves borrowing and selling securities in the hope that they can be bought back at a lower price in the future to close out the short position at a profit.

rules.detail: Lending out Company securities is not addressed; the short-selling definition refers only to a short-seller borrowing securities, not to holders lending them.
CFDs are not named, but a short-term derivative dealing is captured as an example of short-term trading (forward contracts named as an example) for all Employees.
rules.evidence: Short-term trading includes buying and selling securities on market within a 3 month period, and entering into other short term dealings (for example, forward contracts).

rules.detail: A longer-dated CFD over vested, unlocked shares that is not short-term/speculative would be assessed as hedging, requiring prior approval; a short-term CFD remains banned regardless of approval.

rules.detail: Absolute, unqualified prohibition on all Employees entering a margin lending arrangement or transferring securities into an existing margin loan; no vesting distinction and no consent or exceptional-circumstances route at all.
rules.evidence: All Employees are prohibited from: (a) entering into a margin lending arrangement in respect of the Company's securities; and (b) transferring securities in the Company into an existing margin loan.

rules.detail: The policy names only 'margin lending arrangements' (4.5); it does not expressly address granting a charge, mortgage or pledge over Company securities to secure financing that is not structured as a margin loan.

Only margin lending arrangements are named, but the ban is absolute and the Policy takes a 'substance over form' approach, so a bespoke bank loan secured on the shares that is economically equivalent to a margin loan is likely to be treated the same way even if not styled as one.

exemption_authority: The relevant approver under section 5.4's routing table may grant approval to deal during a blackout period in exceptional circumstances (severe financial hardship or compulsion by court order) provided the Restricted Person is not in possession of inside information and provides sufficient evidence the dealing is the most reasonable course available. Approval is not guaranteed to be given, is not obliged to include reasons, can be revoked at any time, and refusal or revocation must be kept confidential.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Company will take a substance over form approach and will have regard to the intent and spirit of this Policy when applying and enforcing it.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even though only 'margin lending arrangements' are named in section 4.5, a bespoke bank loan secured on the collared shares that achieves the same economic effect is likely to be treated as caught by the same absolute prohibition, regardless of how it is documented.

bespoke_clauses.topic: absolute margin lending ban, no carve-out
bespoke_clauses.clause: All Employees are prohibited from: (a) entering into a margin lending arrangement in respect of the Company's securities; and (b) transferring securities in the Company into an existing margin loan.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This is a blanket ban with no vesting distinction and no consent, clearance or exceptional-circumstances route, unlike the hedging ban in 4.3 — the funded collar's loan leg has no path to approval under this policy if characterised as margin lending or an economic equivalent.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Short-term trading includes buying and selling securities on market within a 3 month period, and entering into other short term dealings (for example, forward contracts).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A monetisation structured as a forward contract risks being treated as short-term dealing regardless of its actual tenor, which is relevant if a collar or its unwind is documented as forward-like.

bespoke_clauses.topic: Front Page Test gates all approvals
bespoke_clauses.clause: Where any approval is required for a dealing under this Policy, approval will not be granted where the dealing would not satisfy the Front Page Test.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even a technically compliant collar or approval request can be refused if it would look like the executive is taking advantage of their position, adding a subjective, unappealable filter on top of the formal rules.

bespoke_clauses.clause: the sale of a significant volume of Company securities (i.e. a volume that represents in excess of 10% of the total shares held by the seller prior to the sale, or a volume to be sold that would be in excess of 10% of the average daily traded volume of the shares of the Company on the ASX for the preceding 20 trading days) by a Director needs to be approved by the Board prior to any sale.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unwinding or settling a sizeable collar by a Director may separately require Board approval on volume grounds even where ordinary section 5.3/5.4 approval has already been obtained.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Restricted Persons must take appropriate steps to ensure that their "Connected Persons" only deal in securities in circumstances where the Restricted Person to whom they are connected would be permitted to deal under this Policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Structuring the collar or loan through a spouse, family member or controlled entity does not avoid the Policy's restrictions, including the absolute margin lending ban.

bespoke_clauses.clause: (the Policy names only 'margin lending arrangements' in section 4.5; it does not separately address granting a charge, mortgage or pledge over Company securities)
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A non-margin-loan secured facility might arguably sit outside the literal wording of 4.5, but the substance-over-form clause in section 1 makes reliance on that gap risky.

summary: A funded collar over vested, unlocked DroneShield shares held by a Restricted Person is achievable for the derivative legs: hedging that limits economic risk is banned only prior to vesting or while subject to a holding lock (clause 4.3), and once vested and unlocked the put/call dealing needs prior written approval outside a blackout period (or narrow exceptional-circumstances approval within one) and must pass the Front Page Test. The loan secured on the collared shares is a much harder problem: clause 4.5 imposes an absolute, unqualified ban on all Employees entering a margin lending arrangement or transferring shares into an existing margin loan, with no vesting carve-out and no consent route at all, and the Policy's stated 'substance over form' approach means a bespoke bank loan achieving the same economic effect is likely to be treated the same way even if not styled as a margin loan. If a secured facility nonetheless exists, a lender's enforcement sale is expressly excluded from the blackout, approval and short-term dealing rules, so the bank could still liquidate collateral without needing separate clearance. Directors face an added Board-approval layer for any sale exceeding 10% of their own holding or 10% of 20-day average volume, and must confirm every trade to the Joint Company Secretaries by close of business the same day, while Restricted Persons must also ensure family members and controlled entities deal only on the same terms.
